did_you_know.text: Did you know? Solomon began building the house of the Lord on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, at the place where the Lord had appeared to his father David and where David had prepared the site at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
Did you know? The construction of the temple began in the second month, on the second day of the month, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign.
Did you know? The dimensions of the house were sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, according to the first measurement mentioned in the verse.
Did you know? The entrance hall was twenty cubits wide and one hundred twenty cubits high, and it was overlaid inside with pure gold.
Did you know? The main hall was covered with cypress wood and gold, and decorated with palm-tree motifs and chains.
Did you know? The walls of the house were covered with precious stones for splendor, and the gold used in it was called “gold of Parvaim” in the verse.
Did you know? The Most Holy Place was a square room: its length and width were twenty cubits, and it was overlaid with gold weighing six hundred talents.
Did you know? Two cherubim made of wood and overlaid with gold were placed in the Most Holy Place, and their wings together stretched across twenty cubits.
Did you know? The curtain was made of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, with cherubim embroidered on it.
Did you know? The two pillars in front of the temple were called Jachin—the pillar on the right—and Boaz—the pillar on the left.
